source.author: Al Brooks
source.chapter_title: Failed Breakouts, Breakout Pullbacks, and Breakout Tests

conventions: stop entries mechanized as signal-bar-close then next-bar-open; every tunable constant is a parameter; long side only in pseudocode

candidates.name: BullBreakoutAboveSwingHigh
candidates.quote: if there is a bull breakout and then the market pulls back to around the entry price, forms a buy signal bar, and triggers the long
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar closes above the highest high of the prior N bars (breakoutPoint = that highest high).
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutPoint = highest(high, lookback)[1]; close[0] > breakoutPoint
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the swing high

complexity.reason: highest-high window lookup

notes: Same primitive as R08-06; redefined here per-chapter as the convention allows.

candidates.name: FirstPullbackBarAfterBreakout
candidates.quote: if there is a bull breakout, the first bar with a low below the low of the prior bar is a pullback
candidates.description: Shared primitive: since the most recent bull breakout bar, the first bar whose low is below the prior bar's low marks the start of the pullback.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceBreakout = ctx.BarsSince(R05-01); low[0] < low[1] && noEarlierBarSinceBreakoutHadLowerLow(barsSinceBreakout)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state marker for the pullback)

complexity.reason: must remember the breakout bar and scan forward for the first qualifying bar, not just a two-bar comparison

candidates.name: BullReversalBar
candidates.quote: If instead it is a strong bull reversal bar, chances are the failed breakout will not succeed, and this bull reversal bar then becomes a signal bar for a breakout pullback buy at one tick above its high.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: the current bar makes a new low over a short window yet closes strongly in the upper part of its range and above its open (a bull reversal bar); mirrored for a bear reversal bar making a new high and closing weak.
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] <= lowest(low, reversalLookback)[1] && close[0] > open[0] && (close[0] - low[0]) >= reversalCloseFraction * (high[0] - low[0])
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (bar classification used as a signal-bar test)

complexity.reason: single-bar close-location arithmetic plus a lowest-low window

notes: Brooks gives no numeric fraction for 'strong'; reversalCloseFraction is a reading of it.

candidates.name: BreakoutPullbackTestBuyEntry
candidates.quote: If the breakout pullback comes back to within a few ticks of the entry price, it is a breakout test. The test can occur on the bar after the breakout or even 20 or more bars later... smart traders look to place a buy stop entry order at one tick above it
candidates.description: After a bull breakout and pullback, once the pullback low comes within toleranceTicks of the breakout point, buy one tick above the current (signal) bar's high.
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutPoint = highest(high, lookback)[legStart]; pullbackLow = lowest(low, pullbackWindowBars); (pullbackLow - breakoutPoint) <= toleranceTicks * tickSize && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop one tick above the test/signal bar

complexity.reason: the breakout point must persist and be tested arbitrarily many bars later; the book says a test can occur 20+ bars after the breakout

notes: Distinct from R08-07's very-next-bar 'measuring gap hold' test: this pullback can be deep and far later.

candidates.name: FailedBreakoutReversalEntry
candidates.quote: If the setup or the breakout was weak, and if a strong bear reversal bar developed shortly after the breakout, traders will expect the breakout to fail and for the bear trend to begin or resume.
candidates.description: Within failureWindowBars bars after a bull breakout, a strong bear reversal bar forms and closes back below the breakout point: enter short (the breakout has failed).
candidates.pseudocode: breakoutPoint = highest(high, lookback)[legStart]; ctx.BarsSince(R05-01) <= failureWindowBars && BearReversalBarMirrorOfR05-03[0] && close[0] < breakoutPoint
candidates.book_order_type: sell stop below the reversal bar's low

complexity.reason: cross-bar state: a remembered breakout point tested against a bars-since-breakout window

candidates.name: ReverseToLongOnBullReversalAfterFailedFade
candidates.quote: If you short below the low of that bar and the next bar is a strong bull reversal bar, you usually should reverse back to long because that failed breakout might be failing and instead setting up a breakout pullback buy setup.
candidates.description: While short from a failed-breakout fade entry, if the very next bar is a strong bull reversal bar, reverse the position to long.
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MarketPosition() < 0 && R05-03[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the bull reversal bar, closing and reversing the short

complexity.reason: reads position state in addition to the reversal-bar primitive

notes: An Entry that permits/encourages a reversal rather than a fresh flat entry, like FlatOrOpenLossExceeds but gated on the reversal-bar pattern instead of an open-loss threshold.

candidates.name: StrongTrendCharacteristicsFilter
candidates.quote: important features of a strong bull trend are several consecutive bull trend bars with very little overlap of the bodies, small tails, and bull strength earlier in the day
candidates.description: Context filter: trust a with-trend breakout's follow-through more when recent bars show several consecutive trend bars with small overlap and small tails.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveTrendBars(bodyFraction) >= minConsecutive && avgBarOverlap(overlapWindow) <= maxOverlapFraction && avgTailFraction(overlapWindow) <= maxTailFraction
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: compound window statistics over bar overlap and tail size, plus a consecutive-bar count

notes: Brooks gives no numeric thresholds here; full definition is in the companion Trends volume.

candidates.name: TightRangeOneBarBreakoutUnreliable
candidates.quote: A one-bar breakout of a tight trading range is as likely to fail and reverse back into the range as it is to continue into a trend.
candidates.description: Filter: treat a breakout from a narrow (tight) recent range as low-confidence; require confirmation before trusting it as a trend start.
candidates.pseudocode: rangeHeight = highest(high, rangeLookback) - lowest(low, rangeLookback); rangeHeight <= tightAtrMultiple * atr(atrLookback)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (reliability filter)

complexity.reason: 'tight trading range' is a design decision (boundary detection); the ATR-band proxy is one reading of it

notes: Chapter 22 (Tight Trading Ranges) should be checked for a more authoritative mechanical definition.

candidates.name: OpeningBreakoutFadeTendency
candidates.quote: Sharp breakouts on the open that last for a few bars often fail and lead to a trend day in the opposite direction.
candidates.description: Filter/context: near the session open, treat a sharp breakout as more likely to fail and reverse into an opposite trend day than to continue.
candidates.pseudocode: barsSinceSessionOpen(sessionOpenTime) <= openingWindowBars && strongBreakoutBar[0]
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: 'trend day' and 'a few bars' are fuzzy; needs a design decision before coding

notes: Brooks says this is covered fully in book 3's first-hour-of-trading chapter.

candidates.name: FadeExhaustedCounterSpikeAtSupport
candidates.quote: bulls will aggressively buy around the low and close of the bear spike, which is always down to a support area like a trend line. They are correctly betting that the odds are that the bear breakout will fail and the bull trend will resume.
candidates.description: In an established bull trend, after a sharp countertrend bear spike of spikeBars or more consecutive bear trend bars reaches a support level (moving average), buy near the close of the spike.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveBearTrendBars(bodyFraction) >= spikeBars && low[0] <= ema(emaLength) + supportAtr * atr(atrLookback) && close[0] > open[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy near the close of the spike / buy stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs an established-trend context plus a support-level (trend line or moving average) test

notes: Book's example is a news-driven overnight gap down in an uptrend; the mechanical form drops the news cause and keeps the spike-into-support structure.

candidates.name: ConsecutiveClimaxTwoLegCorrectionFilter
candidates.quote: Bars 1, 2, 3, and 5 ended bear spikes, and consecutive sell climaxes often lead to a correction that lasts at least 10 bars and has at least two legs.
candidates.description: Filter: after climaxesRequired consecutive sell (or buy) climax bars, expect a correction of at least minCorrectionBars bars with at least two legs; block fresh with-trend entries and favor the countertrend side for that stretch.
candidates.pseudocode: consecutiveClimaxCount(climaxAtrMultiple, atrLookback) >= climaxesRequired => blockWithTrendEntry for minCorrectionBars bars
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (context filter)

complexity.reason: leg counting has no agreed mechanical definition; 'climax' itself needs a design decision

notes: Closely related to R08-16 (TwoLegsThenTwoLegCorrection); dedup pass should compare.

candidates.name: DoubleTopBearReversalEntry
candidates.quote: The buyers made two attempts to go above this area and failed both times, creating a double top, so the market should have at least two legs down.
candidates.description: Long-side mirror (double bottom): the current swing low is approximately equal to a prior swing low within toleranceTicks and the bar reverses up; enter long (mirrors a double-top short after two failed attempts at a swing high).
candidates.pseudocode: priorSwingLow = mostRecentSwingLow(pivotStrength, lookback); abs(low[0] - priorSwingLow) <= toleranceTicks * tickSize && BullReversalBarMirror[0]
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the reversal bar

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection to identify the prior swing extreme

notes: Book notes double tops/bottoms 'do not have to be exact.'

candidates.name: TwoBarReversalPrimitive
candidates.quote: They sold below the low of the bear inside bar that followed bar 8 (it formed a two-bar reversal with bar 8).
candidates.description: Shared primitive: a bear trend bar followed by a bull trend bar (or bull inside bar) of comparable size that closes back above the bear bar's midpoint.
candidates.pseudocode: close[1] < open[1] && close[0] > (high[1] + low[1]) / 2 && (high[0] - low[0]) >= sizeRatio * (high[1] - low[1])
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the second bar's high

complexity.reason: two-bar OHLC arithmetic

notes: Same idea as R08-21, redefined here with a looser sizeRatio since this instance is a bear inside bar, not necessarily a full trend bar.

candidates.name: ProtectiveStopBelowEntryBarLow
candidates.quote: The low of the entry bar. If the market falls below the entry bar, it often does so in a strong bear trend bar, and the move down from there is usually big enough for at least a scalp.
candidates.description: Exit the long if price trades below the low of the bar on which the position was entered (a natural stop/failure level distinct from the signal bar).
candidates.pseudocode: low[0] < ctx.EntryBarLow() - toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: protective sell stop at the entry bar's low

complexity.reason: needs to remember the specific entry bar's low, not just the entry price

notes: ctx.EntryBarLow() is a new accessor; the engine currently exposes EntryPrice but not the entry bar's own low/high.

candidates.name: BreakevenStopBuffer
candidates.quote: After an initial run, many traders will take partial profits and then place a breakeven stop on the balance... the trader might place a breakeven stop at 30 cents beyond the breakout, even though it would result in at least a 30 cent loss
candidates.description: Once the position has been profitable by at least triggerTicks, move the stop for the remainder of the position to entry price minus bufferTicks (a 'breakeven' stop that may still take a small loss).
candidates.pseudocode: ctx.MaxPositionProfit() >= triggerTicks * tickSize && low[0] <= ctx.EntryPrice() - bufferTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: breakeven-plus-buffer protective stop

complexity.reason: needs entry price plus the position's peak profit

notes: Distinct from ProfitProtector: the floor is fixed at (near) entry price rather than a retracement fraction of peak profit.

candidates.name: TrailingStopBeyondFailedTestBar
candidates.quote: Once the market falls below the breakout test bar, move the protective stop to 1 cent above its high.
candidates.description: After a breakout-pullback test bar fails to violate the trade (price does not make a new extreme through it), move the protective stop just beyond that test bar's extreme.
candidates.pseudocode: testBarLow = mostRecentFailedTestBarLow(); stopPrice = testBarLow - toleranceTicks * tickSize; low[0] <= stopPrice
candidates.book_order_type: trailing protective stop beyond the last failed test bar

complexity.reason: needs to remember the most recent qualifying test bar's extreme

candidates.name: PullbackLegCountPrimitive
candidates.quote: This higher low was the second attempt for the buyers to take control of the market in this price area and they succeeded, so there should be at least two legs up.
candidates.description: Shared primitive: count the number of distinct down-legs (pullback legs) since the last swing high in an up move, where a new leg begins each time price makes a lower low pivot after having made a higher high pivot.
candidates.pseudocode: legCount = countLegsSinceSwingHigh(pivotStrength, lookback)
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (state used by H1/H2/L1/L2 setups)

complexity.reason: needs swing-pivot detection and a persistent leg counter

notes: Underlies H1/H2 (and by mirror, L1/L2), the bar-counting setups formally covered in Chapter 17.

candidates.name: H1PullbackBuyEntry
candidates.quote: When there is strong momentum, buying a high 1 pullback is a good trade.
candidates.description: In an up leg, after exactly one pullback leg since the most recent swing high, buy one tick above the high of the pullback (signal) bar.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the pullback signal bar

complexity.reason: depends on the leg-count primitive's pivot detection

notes: Mirrors to L1 on the short side per the sides convention.

candidates.name: H2PullbackBuyEntry
candidates.quote: There was a second long entry at bar 6, which was a high 2. In strong trends, sometimes the high 2 entry is higher than that of the high 1 (here, three bars earlier).
candidates.description: In an up leg, after exactly two pullback legs since the most recent swing high, buy one tick above the high of the second pullback (signal) bar.
candidates.book_order_type: buy stop above the pullback signal bar

complexity.reason: depends on the leg-count primitive's pivot detection

notes: Mirrors to L2 on the short side. Chapter 17 (bar counting high/low 1 2 3 4) should be checked for the book's canonical definition.

candidates.name: StairsPatternHigherLowFilter
candidates.quote: That breakout pullback stays above the prior higher low, creating a bull trend of higher highs and lows, and then is followed by another higher high.
candidates.description: Filter: confirm a bull 'stairs' structure is intact by requiring the most recent pullback low to stay above the prior swing low (a rising sequence of higher lows).
candidates.pseudocode: priorSwingLow = mostRecentSwingLow(pivotStrength, lookback)[1]; low[0] > priorSwingLow
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (structure filter)

complexity.reason: needs a remembered prior swing low; the comparison itself is trivial once pivots exist

candidates.name: WedgeThirdPushRetestTarget
candidates.quote: After the market rallies to the third push up in a potential wedge (a rising convergent channel), the odds are very high that it will test the top of the second push up. Once it reverses, it usually tests to the bottom of the wedge
candidates.description: After a three-push wedge top forms, expect the subsequent pullback/reversal to retest the top of the second push, and beyond that the bottom of the first pullback (wedge channel bottom); exit or take profit on a countertrend trade there.
candidates.pseudocode: secondPushTop = pushHigh(pushIndex=2); low[0] <= secondPushTop + toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit near the second push top

complexity.reason: needs three-push/wedge recognition from swing pivots

notes: Chapter 18 (wedge and three-push pullbacks) should have the canonical mechanical definition.

candidates.name: SpikeTopRetestAfterChannelBreak
candidates.quote: The top of a spike in a spike and channel bull trend. Once the market breaks below the channel, it usually tests down to the top of the spike, and eventually to the bottom of the channel.
candidates.description: After a spike-and-channel bull trend's channel breaks (a close below the channel line), expect the decline to retest the top of the original spike, then the bottom of the channel.
candidates.pseudocode: spikeTop = high of the last bar of the identified spike; channelBroken && low[0] <= spikeTop + toleranceTicks * tickSize
candidates.book_order_type: profit-taking limit / countertrend target at the spike top

complexity.reason: needs spike and channel-line detection/projection

candidates.name: FinalFlagChannelProjectionContinuation
candidates.quote: the channel that contained the final bear flag, if projected up and to the right, will sometimes also approximately contain the new bull trend.
candidates.description: After a trend reversal where the prior trend's final flag was itself a shallow channel, project that channel's slope forward as an approximate boundary/target-continuation zone for the new opposite trend; swing more of the position while price stays within it.
candidates.pseudocode: projectedChannel = projectChannel(finalFlagChannelLine, forwardBars); close[0] within projectedChannel => holdPosition
candidates.book_order_type: n/a (position-sizing/hold guidance, not an order)

complexity.reason: channel projection plus a subjective 'approximately contains' test; needs a design decision on tolerance

notes: Speculative even by the book's own hedge ('sometimes...approximately'); low-priority for authoring.

rejected.quote: On daily charts, there are often sharp countertrend breakouts due to surprising news events.
rejected.reason: news events are data the engine does not have

rejected.quote: if you were trading the 3 minute chart, you would have seen that the bar 6 high was a breakout test of the 3 minute bar that formed the high at bar 3 above
rejected.reason: requires a second, faster-timeframe bar series not available to a single-timeframe rule

rejected.quote: Traders should concentrate on trading the bigger turning points, like bars 4, 7, 9, and 12.
rejected.reason: pure discretion about trade selection, no bar-level test

chapter_summary: Chapter on the breakout/failed-breakout/breakout-pullback/breakout-test cycle that recurs constantly in Brooks's framework. It defines the core primitives (bull breakout above a swing high, first pullback bar, bull/bear reversal bar, two-bar reversal) and builds from them the breakout-pullback continuation entry, the failed-breakout reversal entry, and the reversal-of-a-reversal permission. It also lists a long catalog of common pullback destinations (breakout point, spike top, wedge second-push top, entry-bar low, swing low at the leg start, moving average/trend line support) which are graded hard/research since they need swing-pivot and channel/wedge detection; several are near-duplicates of Chapter 8's measured-move and magnet primitives, and the dedup pass should merge them. H1/H2 pullback entries are introduced here in passing (formal treatment is Chapter 17) and defined via a shared, admittedly hard-to-implement leg-count primitive. Two management rules (breakeven-stop buffer, trailing stop beyond a failed test bar) round out the Exit side. Most of the chapter is discretionary chart narration (specific bar-by-bar walkthroughs of figures); only the passages restated above as candidates are rule-like.
